cells.note: Initial mount / populated render OK (ExampleCard via getExamples-derived ExampleInfo[]; collapsed read-only clamped expex editor #43). Empty state OK (ExamplesPanel.tsx:86-91). But: (a) preview truncation is purely CSS height-clamp over a CSS grid — a \pex with a body paragraph + multiple \a items clips to a sliver showing only (N) at 1-line docked clamp (ExampleCard.tsx:334-343, useCompressedLines docked=1); (b) per-collapsed-card a FULL read-only TipTap editor is mounted (N editors for N collapsed cards, acknowledged #43 ExampleCard.tsx:430-433) — mount-footprint, not a keystroke regression. See EX-F1-01, EX-F1-02.

Editable example body mounts a SEPARATE embedded editor (buildEditorExtensions surface:float). Citation/footnote atom click-through WORKS (their NodeViews dispatch window events unconditionally — citation.ts:261, footnote.ts:271). But inline/display MATH is inert: math.ts:73 `if (surface !== "main") return` suppresses virgil-math-click on every float surface, so clicking math in the example card body opens no editor (EX-F4-02). \ref (LabelRef) IS clickable (label.ts:53, not surface-gated) but marker-clicks.ts:333 anchors the ref popover via a GLOBAL document.querySelector('.label-ref-node[data-label]') that returns the FIRST match — when the same label is also referenced in main text, the popover anchors to the wrong element (EX-F4-01). Read-only fallback (BorrowedMainText) is dead in production (editor context always present). Citation alignment sourceEl querySelector has the same first-match ambiguity (EX-F4-03).

Edit body WORKS (directly-editable expex editor writes back via writeBackToMain). BUT two defects on that path: write-back sets addToHistory:false (ExampleCard.tsx:197) so card-body edits are NOT undoable in the main editor (EX-F5-02); and the nodeFromJSON write-back is wrapped in a silent `catch {}` (ExampleCard.tsx:200) so a schema-invalid edit silently fails to reach the doc → card↔doc divergence (EX-F5-03). TITLE EDIT is entirely unwired: ExampleCard renders no title/+T, ExampleInfo carries no title field, useExamples (updateExampleTitle/deleteExample/syncFromEditor + the BUG#31 isAutoTitle strip) is NEVER invoked anywhere in the app — dead code over an unreachable examples.json sidecar (R2) (EX-F5-01). AI-request flag N-A for examples per subject map.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: An example card's title can never be edited or displayed, and the examples.json sidecar (title + createdAt persistence) is never written or read — the entire useExamples hook is dead code.
findings.suspectedRootCause: useExamples(docId) is never invoked by any component (grep: only referenced in comments + the hook file itself). The two panel hosts that actually render examples — ExamplesPanelHost (EditorPane.tsx:5659, the main-app docked panel) and buildExampleOmniItems (omni.tsx, the main-app omni column) — both thread only the editor-derived ExampleInfo[] (no `title`), `selectedId`/`selectedExampleId`, `onSelect`, and `onJump`. Neither wires updateExampleTitle, deleteExample, syncFromEditor, or onAdd. ExampleInfo (Editor.tsx:193-221) has no `title` field, and ExampleCard.tsx renders no CardBodyTitle / bodyTitle. So the sidecar metadata layer the hook implements has no surface. The codebase even documents this state: cards/types.ts:177 and cards/floats/index.tsx:24 call it 'no reachable ExampleRef sidecar (R2)'.

evidence.note: useExamples defined but never imported/called by any component (only comment references elsewhere).
ExamplesPanelHost (main-app docked panel) wires only examples/selectedId(local useState)/onSelect/onJump — no title-edit, delete, or add; never calls useExamples.
buildExampleOmniItems (main-app omni surface) passes only examples/selectedExampleId/setSelectedExampleId/onJump — no title-edit or delete.
ExampleCard renders no CardBodyTitle/bodyTitle and references no example.title — title is never shown nor editable.
ExampleInfo has no title field, so even if a sidecar title existed it isn't merged into the card's data shape.

reproSteps: Open a paper with an \ex/\pex example.
Open the Examples panel (or omni) — the example card shows the expex body but no title affordance (no +T, no editable title input).
There is no path in the UI to set or persist an example title; examples.json is never written.
findings.suspectedClass: Hook-without-a-consumer dead code: any per-doc sidecar hook (useTodos/useReports/useArchive) wired through a panel host that drops its mutators would silently disable that panel's persistence. Worth auditing each *PanelHost in EditorPane.tsx for dropped hook outputs.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: Edits typed directly into an example card's body cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z in the main editor.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The card body's write-back to the main doc tags its transaction with `tr.setMeta('addToHistory', false)` (ExampleCard.tsx:197) — copied verbatim from the in-editor example float ('parity with the float'). For a popped float that mirrors a doc the user is also editing in place, suppressing history avoids double-recording; but the example card body is a primary directly-editable surface (#32/#33). Every keystroke in the card writes back history-suppressed, so the main editor's undo stack never records the change. A subsequent main-text edit + undo will skip past the card edits, and the user has no way to revert what they typed in the card.

evidence.note: writeBackToMain: tr.setMeta('addToHistory', false) on the replaceWith transaction.
onUpdate fires writeBackToMain(ed.getJSON()) on every embedded-editor change — so all card-body typing rides the history-suppressed write-back.

reproSteps: Open the Examples panel, expand an example card.
Type text into the example body inside the card.
Focus the main editor and press Ctrl+Z — the card-body edit is not undone (it was never added to history).
findings.suspectedClass: Any directly-editable card body that writes back to the main doc with addToHistory:false loses undo. The example float pattern (text-objects/floats/example-block-body.tsx) shares this and is defensible for a float; the question is whether a primary editable card surface should differ. Check other FLOAT_WRITE_META writers for the same history loss when the surface is a card rather than a float.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: An example-body edit that produces schema-invalid expex JSON is silently dropped from the main doc — the card shows the new content but the document never receives it (until a re-seed reverts the card).
findings.suspectedRootCause: writeBackToMain wraps `ed.state.schema.nodeFromJSON(...)` + dispatch in a bare `try { ... } catch { /* swallow */ }` (ExampleCard.tsx:187-202). If the embedded editor's serialized JSON fails to rebuild as a valid exampleBlock node (stale uuid, malformed gloss/xlist nesting, attr mismatch), the catch swallows it with no user feedback and no error. The card's local editor still shows the edit, so the user believes it landed; the main doc is unchanged. On the next rev.examples/contentRev re-seed (ExampleCard.tsx:268-299) the card silently reverts to the doc's content, discarding the user's edit.

evidence.note: try { nodeFromJSON + replaceWith + dispatch } ...
catch { /* schema mismatch / stale uuid — swallow */ } — no user-visible error, write silently lost.
re-seed effect compares serialized JSON and setContent's the live block back into the card, reverting the swallowed edit on the next structural/content signal.

reproSteps: Edit an example body in the card in a way that yields invalid expex node JSON (e.g. an edit the float schema can't reconstruct).
The card displays the edit but writeBackToMain's nodeFromJSON throws and is swallowed — the doc is untouched.
Trigger a re-seed (add/remove any example, or a content edit to this example from elsewhere) — the card reverts, losing the typed content with no warning.
findings.suspectedClass: Silent swallow-on-write-back: the same try/catch-swallow appears in the example float (intentional parity). Lead #9's 'swallowed schema errors'. Any card/float that writes back via nodeFromJSON inside a bare catch can silently diverge from the doc — audit FLOAT_WRITE_META write-back sites for surfaced-vs-swallowed errors.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: Clicking a \ref inside an example card body can open the ref-edit popover anchored to a DIFFERENT ref of the same label in the main text, not the one clicked.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The LabelRef NodeView (label.ts:53-65) dispatches virgil-label-ref-click with only the label string in detail — no position/element identity. The bridge (marker-clicks.ts:333) resolves the anchor element by a GLOBAL document.querySelector('.label-ref-node[data-label="<label>"]'), which returns the FIRST matching element in DOM order. The example card body is a second editor whose DOM also contains a .label-ref-node for the same label (the card is seeded from a copy of the block). If the same label is also \ref'd in main text, querySelector matches whichever is earlier in the DOM — typically the main-text ref — so the popover's rect/setActiveRefRect points at the wrong instance.

evidence.note: LabelRef click dispatches virgil-label-ref-click from ANY surface (not surface-gated, unlike math).
handler resolves anchor via global document.querySelector('.label-ref-node[data-label=...]') — first match wins, ambiguous across main + card-body copies.

reproSteps: Have a label that is \ref'd in main text AND inside an example whose body is shown in an example card.
Click the \ref rendered inside the example card body.
The ref popover opens anchored to the main-text ref instead of the clicked card-body ref.
findings.suspectedClass: Global-querySelector-by-shared-key after a click that originated in an embedded/duplicate editor. The citation alignment path (EX-F4-03) has the same shape. Any bridge that re-resolves the clicked element by a global attribute selector instead of carrying the element/rect in the event will mis-target when the same atom id/label exists in more than one mounted editor (card body, omni copy, float copy).

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: Clicking inline or display math inside an example card body does nothing — no math editor/popover opens, so math nested in an example can't be edited from the card.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The example card body mounts buildEditorExtensions({surface:'float'}); the InlineMath/DisplayMath NodeViews are configured surface:'float' (editor-extensions.ts:1752-1753), and the math click handler bails on any non-main surface (math.ts:73 `if (surface !== 'main') return`). This is deliberate for floats (a float's getPos indexes the float doc, so firing virgil-math-click would mis-target MAIN by position). The side effect is that the directly-editable example card body — which users reasonably expect to be a full editing surface — silently swallows math clicks. Math is an atom (not free-text), so there's also no inline keyboard edit path; the only way to edit example math is the code/source view.

evidence.note: InlineMath.configure({ surface: isFloat ? 'float' : 'main' }) — example card body is isFloat=true.
click handler: if (surface !== 'main') return; — inert in every float, incl. the example card body.

reproSteps: Open an example containing inline math (\ex with $...$) in the Examples panel; expand the card.
Click the rendered math inside the card body.
Nothing happens — no math popover; the math cannot be edited from the card.
findings.suspectedClass: Surface-gated atom interactivity vs. card-as-editable-surface tension: the example card body is the one float-surface editor that is also a primary editing surface, so the 'inert in every float' rule under-serves it. Any other atom whose interactivity is gated to surface:'main' (vs. carrying a host/position remap) is similarly dead inside the example card body.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: Clicking a citation inside an example card body may vertically align the citation card to the wrong on-screen citation instance.
findings.suspectedRootCause: virgil-citation-click is handled by selecting the citation and calling alignOmniCardWithClick with a sourceEl resolved via a global document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id="<id>"]') (marker-clicks.ts:319-321). The example card body is a separate editor whose DOM also holds a .citation-node with the same citationId (seeded from the block copy), so the first-match query can return the card-body copy or the main-text copy depending on DOM order — the alignment math then references the wrong element. (Selection + card-open are correct; only the click-Y alignment can be off.) Note: the NodeView also passes clickedPos=getPos() in the float's coordinate space, but that detail field is never consumed (citation.ts:281; no reader in marker-clicks.ts), so it causes no mis-targeting itself.

evidence.note: sourceEl = document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id=...]') — first match across main + card-body copies.
clickedPos=getPos() dispatched in the embedded editor's coordinate space, but unconsumed downstream.

reproSteps: Have a citation that appears both in main text and inside an example whose body shows in a card.
Click the citation inside the example card body.
The citation card selects correctly but may align to the main-text citation's Y rather than the clicked one.
findings.suspectedClass: Same global-querySelector-by-shared-key class as EX-F4-01. The fix shape (carry the clicked element/rect in the event) would resolve both.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: The collapsed preview of a multi-part example (\pex with a body paragraph + several \a items, or a long interlinear gloss) clips to a tiny sliver — often just '(N)' and a fragment of the first line.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The collapsed example preview renders the FULL read-only expex editor and clamps it by a fixed maxHeight = calc(var(--editor-line-height,1.8) * 1em * clampLines), clampLines = useCompressedLines() (docked=1, omni=2) (ExampleCard.tsx:334-343, card-display.tsx:28-29). Because the expex content is a CSS grid (not text flow), the comment correctly notes -webkit-line-clamp can't be used, so it just hard-caps height and overflow:hidden. For a single short \ex this is fine, but a \pex's number row + body + multiple sub-item rows + gloss rows are far taller than 1-2 lines, so the clamp clips after the first line — the preview conveys almost nothing about the example.

evidence.note: maxHeight clamp over the expex grid at clampLines prose lines, overflow:hidden.
DOCKED_COMPRESSED_LINES=1 — a single line ceiling for a multi-row expex grid.

reproSteps: Open a paper with a \pex example that has a top body line plus 2-3 \a sub-items (or a \begingl gloss).
View it collapsed in the docked Examples panel (1-line clamp).
The preview shows only the (N) and a sliver of the first row; sub-items/gloss are clipped.
findings.suspectedClass: Line-count clamp applied to non-text-flow (grid) content: any borrowed-body kind that renders structured (non-paragraph) content under compressedBodyStyle's height ceiling will clip unhelpfully. Worth checking figure/graphics block previews and any future structured card body.

findings.subject: examples
findings.symptom: Every collapsed example card mounts a full (read-only) TipTap editor; a panel/omni with N collapsed example cards holds N live embedded editors.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Since #43 the collapsed preview renders through the SAME ExampleCardEditor (read-only + height-clamped) as the expanded body, rather than a static string, to keep collapsed≡expanded rendering parity (ExampleCard.tsx:434-444, 426-433). The comment explicitly acknowledges this mount footprint. It is NOT a keystroke-sanctity regression (the editors re-seed only on rev.examples/contentRev, never per keystroke — pinned by ExampleCardEditor.test.tsx 'keystroke sanctity'), but it is a real memory/CPU cost that scales with the number of examples and informs any future panel/omni virtualization. Flagged as a verified non-keystroke footprint cost, not a correctness bug.

evidence.note: Mount-footprint note (#43): N embedded read-only editors for N collapsed cards.
collapsed branch mounts ExampleCardEditor (readOnly, clampLines) rather than a static summary string.

reproSteps: Open a paper with many (e.g. 20+) examples.
View the Examples panel / omni with all cards collapsed.
20+ embedded TipTap editors are mounted simultaneously (one per collapsed card).
findings.suspectedClass: Per-card embedded-editor mount as the default collapsed renderer: any card kind that renders its collapsed preview through a real editor (vs. a string) scales editor count with list length. Examples is the only borrowed-body kind doing this for collapsed previews today.
